analysis.title: GS Johnstone - GS TMT SPEC SALES: Semis 4th largest SOX drawdown since 99; Cutting memory estimates; State of Software; Crowdstrike Zscaler; Amazon
key_insights: GS Vol Panic Index closed Friday at 9.8/10. Historically such readings were good entries for adding risk, but this time the Fed is hiking and hedge funds are de-risking and adding shorts.

SOX is down ~43% from its June 2026 peak, the fourth-largest drawdown since 1999 behind dot-com (-83%), GFC (-66%) and 2022 (-46%). It has exceeded the mid-cycle range (avg -24%, worst -31%) and behaves like a full cycle downturn, though SOX is still up 18% YTD.
So far the semis move is a de-rating, not an earnings downturn. GIR cut 2028 memory estimates: conventional DRAM now +32%/-19% YoY in 2027E/2028E (from +32%/-5%), NAND +20%/-21% (from +30%/-14%).
GIR cut Samsung 2028E operating profit by 26% and SK Hynix by 23%. Price targets fall to W350k from W500k (Samsung) and W2.0m from W3.5m (SK Hynix), both stay Buy as downside is seen as priced in.

GIR says Samsung and SK Hynix shares price in zero AI capex growth in 2028E and ASPs 40% below base case. LTA defaults need conventional DRAM prices 32-54% below base case. Samsung downside case implies 4.7x P/E and 1.0x P/B.
HBM remains the bright spot: GIR raised HBM TAM to US$60bn/US$200bn/US$237bn in 2026E/2027E/2028E. CXMT estimates were cut for 2026-30E.
Credit stress: SpaceX's $32B+ SPV/lease deal shows chip financing is available only at >8%. Neoclouds (CRWV, NBIS) show 15% unsecured yields and 1,200 bp CDS. Hyperscaler CDS widened, ORCL widest.

Prime brokerage data through Thursday showed a third straight week of net global equity selling. Short sales outpaced long buys 1.5 to 1, the highest since April 2025. Weekly shorting was the largest since June 2022. Short-covering fuel exists but de-grossing may not be done.
Policy: Bessent distinguished commercial chip sales to China from sales to the Chinese military, and Trump supported domestic chip manufacturing. Read as a policy safety net for semis.

Enterprise software: GIR is more positive on cybersecurity and select AI beneficiaries (Microsoft, MongoDB, Palantir, Snowflake) and more cautious on traditional application software facing tougher renewals and AI-native challengers.
CrowdStrike is reportedly in talks to buy Zscaler for over $50bn. CRWD fell ~10% after hours and ZS rose 16-19%. The deal would face 12-18 months of antitrust review.
Amazon: GIR reiterates Buy and $370 12-month PT, calling it the most compelling risk/reward in mega/large cap coverage, with AWS growth framed at 40%+ YoY in 2027 and 2028.
AI server OEMs (Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro) reportedly seek post-contract price hikes of up to 45% on memory costs. GPU server prices are up 20-30% and some CPU server prices tripled (FT).

US tape: SPX retested 7k after a 7th straight down session, down ~8.6% on the week, the second-worst week since Covid. Nasdaq VIX is at its highest since COVID. Top-of-book liquidity in S&P was $4mm, near YTD low.
CTAs are net short -$19bn US equity length (26th percentile) after selling $57bn in a month, and are forecast to sell in every scenario next week. SPX triggers are 7596/7540/7119.

Fundamental L/S funds fell 2.7% on the week, are up 7.0% YTD (from +17.4% in June). Hedge funds re-grossed by the most in 4+ years after 5 weeks of de-grossing, with long/short ratio at a record low and EM net sold 10 straight weeks.
Worldline fell ~15% on an FT report on historical cash-flow practices, reviving quality-of-earnings concerns. CTS Eventim set 2030 targets above GS and consensus.
Japan semi-cap: stocks near trough multiples despite robust orders. GIR favours Lasertec, Disco, Ebara and Tokyo Electron and is cautious on SCREEN, Tokyo Seimitsu and Ulvac.
SK Hynix will convert SPC2 bonds, giving it a 14.53% voting stake in Kioxia and making it the largest shareholder effective Dec 4, 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Samsung 2028E operating profit cut 26% on weaker DRAM and NAND pricing. GIR sees downside priced in.
SK Hynix 2028E operating profit cut 23%. HBM TAM raised and downside seen as priced in.
Most compelling risk/reward in mega/large cap coverage, with AWS growth framed at 40%+ in 2027 and 2028.
GIR is more positive ahead of earnings on rising security spend. Shares fell ~10% after hours on the reported Zscaler deal.
Shares rose 16-19% after hours on reports of a $50bn+ CrowdStrike bid.
Worldline fell ~15% on FT cash-flow practices report. Company reaffirmed 2026 guidance.
Nemetschek cut to Underweight at JPMorgan (away from GS).
Vodafone cut to Sell at Citi (away from GS).

sector_views.rationale: De-rating so far, not an earnings downturn. Memory 2027 constructive, 2028 cut. Policy backstop and heavy shorting support a bounce.
GIR keeps Buy on Samsung and SK Hynix as 2028 downside is priced in, and HBM TAM is raised.
Outages, ageing infrastructure and AI-driven attacks accelerate security spending.
Tougher renewals and AI-native challengers pressure incumbents.
Near trough multiples with stock selection becoming company-specific.

earnings_insights: CrowdStrike earnings are upcoming, GIR is more positive ahead of the print.
Q3'26 US internet earnings season recap: themes were AI revenue perception, sources and uses of capital, a reversal of agentic commerce, and a stable digital consumer.
CTS Eventim 2030 targets: revenue above €4.5bn (company target, 15% above GSe and 13% above consensus), adjusted EBITDA above €1bn at a 22% margin (29% above GSe, 25% above consensus).
Worldline: PwC estimated ~€200m of the €520m 2022 FCF came from optimisation (per FT). Company reaffirmed 2026 guidance.
GIR stress test: Samsung 2028E revenue 29% below base, operating profit 54% below, net profit 48% below, with a 35% operating margin in the downside case (GIR estimate).

Neocloud credit stress (15% unsecured yields, 1,200 bp CDS) and widening hyperscaler CDS.
NVDA SEC probe headline and Iran strike escalation.
CrowdStrike/Zscaler integration risk and a 12-18 month antitrust review.

Short sales outpaced long buys 1.5 to 1, the highest since April 2025. Weekly shorting was the largest since June 2022 and third largest in a decade.
CTAs net short -$19bn (26th percentile) after selling $57bn over a month. SPX triggers are 7596/7540/7119.

tension_points.bull_case: Extreme sentiment (Vol Panic 9.8/10), heavy shorting, policy backstop and priced-in memory downside support a bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed is hiking, hedge fund de-grossing continues, and 2028 memory estimates are being cut so a de-rating may become an earnings downturn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS watches for one of three bottoming conditions: better AI earnings confidence, a dovish Fed signal, or a major drop in positioning. SPX CTA trigger at 7119.
